Recurrent-Event Cox Models: Andersen-Gill, PWP, Wei-Lin-Weissfeld and Frailty

Source: R/recurrent_events.R
recurrent_cox.Rd

Fits a Cox model to recurrent events in counting-process form, for example repeated hospital readmissions, instead of treating readmission as one binary outcome or stopping at the first event. The data have one row per at-risk interval with a start, a stop and an event indicator ([recurrent_intervals()] builds them from event dates). Standard errors are robust (clustered on the subject) except for `"frailty"`.

Usage

recurrent_cox(
  data,
  predictors,
  id = "id",
  start = "tstart",
  stop = "tstop",
  status = "status",
  model = c("ag", "pwp_total", "pwp_gap", "wlw", "frailty"),
  max_events = NULL,
  min_stratum_events = 10,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of counting-process intervals.

predictors

Covariates: a character vector of column names, or a one-sided formula such as `~ age + sex`.

id, start, stop, status

Column names (strings) of the subject identifier, the interval start and stop, and the event indicator (0/1 or logical).

model

One of `"ag"`, `"pwp_total"`, `"pwp_gap"`, `"wlw"`, `"frailty"`.

max_events

For the stratified models, event numbers above `max_events` are pooled into one stratum (default `NULL`: the largest number with at least `min_stratum_events` events and all below it). Ignored by `"ag"` and `"frailty"`.

min_stratum_events

With `max_events = NULL`, the smallest number of events a stratum needs; later strata are pooled into the last one that has enough (default `10`).

conf_level

Confidence level of the hazard ratios (default `0.95`).

Value

An object of class `recurrent_cox`: a list with `fit` (the [survival::coxph()] fit), `model`, `terms` (a tibble with `term`, `estimate` (log hazard ratio), `std_error`, `hr`, `conf_low`, `conf_high`, `statistic` and `p_value`), `n_subjects`, `n_intervals`, `n_events`, `events_per_subject` (a table), `strata_events` (events per event number, `NULL` for the unstratified models), `frailty_variance` (`NA` unless `"frailty"`) and `conf_level`. `tidy()` returns `terms`.

Details

* `"ag"`, Andersen-Gill: one baseline hazard, events of a subject are independent given the covariates. The hazard ratio is the effect on the rate of events. * `"pwp_total"`, Prentice-Williams-Peterson with total time: a subject is at risk for event `k` only after event `k - 1`, with a baseline hazard per event number (stratified), on the time since time zero. * `"pwp_gap"`: as `"pwp_total"` on the gap time since the previous event. The time scale restarts after each event. * `"wlw"`, Wei-Lin-Weissfeld: marginal model in which a subject is at risk for every event number from time zero; a common effect is estimated over event numbers (stratified by event number). Only the covariates of each subject's first interval (baseline covariates) are used: a predictor that varies within a subject is taken at its first-interval value, with a warning naming it. Use `"pwp_total"` (which uses interval-specific covariates) when the time-varying values matter. * `"frailty"`: Andersen-Gill with a gamma frailty for the subject ([survival::frailty()]), so the variance of the frailty (`frailty_variance`) measures how much subjects differ beyond the covariates.

Rows after an event are valid here: [validate_start_stop()] and [prune_start_stop()] take `recurrent = TRUE` for the same data.

See also

[recurrent_intervals()], [recurrent_cox_windows()], [truncate_start_stop()], [validate_start_stop()], [cox_single()]

Examples

if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  n <- 150
  subj <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n), age = rnorm(n), end = 120)
  ev <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    k <- rpois(1, exp(0.3 * subj$age[i]) * 1.2)
    if (k == 0) return(NULL)
    data.frame(id = i, time = sort(runif(k, 1, 120)))
  }))
  long <- recurrent_intervals(ev, subj)
  long$age <- subj$age[long$id]
  fit <- recurrent_cox(long, ~ age, model = "ag")
  fit
  recurrent_cox(long, "age", model = "pwp_gap")$terms
}
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   term  estimate std_error    hr conf_low conf_high statistic p_value
#>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 age      0.219    0.0766  1.24     1.07      1.45      2.86 0.00430
